learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how we perceive ourselves (Self-concept, Self-esteem) and understand the major psychological theories that explain human personality!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The 'Self' refers to the totality of an individual's conscious experiences, ideas, thoughts, and feelings with regard to themselves. It includes self-concept, self-esteem, self-efficacy, and self-control.

Personality refers to our characteristic ways of responding to individuals and situations. Major approaches include: Type approaches (categorizing people), Trait approaches (persistent attributes), Psychodynamic approaches (Freud's theory of Id, Ego, Superego), and Humanistic approaches (focusing on personal growth).

Sigmund Freud proposed that personality is driven by unconscious forces. The mind has three structures: Id (pleasure principle), Ego (reality principle), and Superego (moral conscience). When anxiety occurs, the ego uses Defense Mechanisms like repression, projection, and rationalization.

Personality is assessed using Self-Report Measures (like questionnaires), Projective Techniques (like Rorschach Inkblot Test, where ambiguous stimuli reveal unconscious desires), and Behavioural Analysis (observation, interview).

fun_activity.title: 🛡️ Spotting Defense Mechanisms
fun_activity.instructions: Think of a time when you blamed bad test results on 'a terrible teacher' instead of studying. Identify this as 'Rationalization'. Try spotting other defense mechanisms (like projection or denial) in movies or daily conversations!

exam_tips: 📌 Freud's structural components of personality (Id, Ego, Superego) and levels of conscious mind (Conscious, Subconscious, Unconscious) are heavily tested.
📌 Know at least 3-4 Defense Mechanisms with real-life examples (e.g., Repression, Projection, Reaction Formation, Rationalization).
📌 Differentiate clearly between Self-Report Inventories and Projective Techniques in terms of structure and subjectivity.
quick_recap: ⭐ The self develops through social interactions and cultural environments.
⭐ Personality theories range from Freud's unconscious dynamics to humanistic emphasis on free will.
⭐ Assessment methods combine structured inventories with unstructured projective tests.
